name: Particle Photos
description: Photographs become living engravings. Disturb the marks, uncover their detail, and let them find their way home.

assets.credit: Original particle treatment of Brandon Burridge’s Tampa photograph

compatibility: Native WebGL2 instanced fragments. No third-party runtime dependencies or imports from the Stories archive.
Canvas 2D renders a smaller interactive engraving when WebGL2 is unavailable or interrupted.
Pointer, keyboard and touch interaction. Reduced motion applies changes immediately without drifting or animated scattering.
Photographs keep their full aspect ratio. Device pixel ratio and texture size are capped; only one image texture is retained per instrument.
Local PNG/JPEG/WebP photos up to 12 MB and 24 megapixels are processed in the browser. Uploads stay in this session and are not included in recipe/source exports.
Original-image toggle, descriptive image labels, HTML field notes, and static no-JavaScript plate remain available.
notes: Every fragment has an anchor and tonal information sampled from the photograph. Luminance and local contrast determine stippling, fine strokes and crosshatched marks.

Pointer movement displaces individual marks. In reveal mode each fragment resolves its own patch of the photograph; no photographic plane or opacity-mask overlay sits underneath it. Leaving the field returns the marks to their anchors.

Scatter and Reassemble control the same instances. Original rendering resolves those instances into a continuous photograph. Photo selection preserves landscape, portrait and unusually wide compositions.
Open field note demonstrates an engraving resolving into an image-led content view. Return brings the same plate back. A separate gallery example is included in the exported source.

Reference studied: Eddy Naboulet’s image-derived, pointer-responsive particle formations. All sampling, shaders, interface and transition code are original; its overall design and assets were not copied.
reuse: Extract the ZIP, serve it over local HTTP, and open example.html. The three demonstration photos, credits and licenses are included.
Use createParticleImage from engine.js for a single image with your own controls. It accepts a decoded image, dimensions, settings and lifecycle callbacks.
Use mount from index.js for the complete instrument. The gallery-demo.html example demonstrates several independently managed images and a content-view transition.
Pause offscreen or hidden instances, and dispose before removal. Read README.md for settings, normalized pointer coordinates, resource limits and source licensing.
